name: Israel

summary.text: This record covers only specific, documented dealings between the Israeli government (including its Ministry of Defense) and U.S. technology companies already on this site. In April 2021 Israel's Finance Ministry selected Amazon Web Services and Google for Project Nimbus, a government cloud project with an initial investment of about 4 billion shekels ($1.2 billion). In January 2024 Palantir, after a board meeting in Tel Aviv, announced a strategic partnership with the Ministry of Defense. In September 2025 Microsoft said it had ceased and disabled specified services to a unit within the Ministry of Defense following an external review.

facts.claim: On April 21, 2021 Israel's Finance Ministry announced that Amazon Web Services and Google had won the Project Nimbus tender to build local cloud sites for the government, with an initial investment of 4 billion shekels (about $1.2 billion); Microsoft, Oracle and IBM lost out. The ministry described the project as a multi-year flagship project providing cloud services to the government, the defense system and other groups in the economy.
facts.quote: The initial investment is 4 billion shekels ($1.2 billion).

sources.title: Amazon's AWS and Google big winners of Israel's $1.2 billion milestone cloud project
Google, AWS win $1.2 billion Israel tender for cloud services
Israel picks Amazon, Google for flagship cloud project

facts.claim: Google has said the Nimbus contract covers workloads running on its commercial cloud by Israeli government ministries that agree to its terms of service and acceptable use policy, and that the work is not directed at highly sensitive, classified or military workloads relevant to weapons or intelligence services.
facts.quote: not directed at highly sensitive, classified, or military workloads relevant to weapons or intelligence services

sources.title: Exclusive: Workers at Google DeepMind Push Company to Drop Military Contracts

facts.claim: The Intercept reported in 2024 and 2025, citing internal Google documents and the contract, that the Israeli government 'may make any use of any service included in the supplier's catalog of services' under Nimbus and that Google was not permitted to restrict the types of services and information that the government, including the Ministry of Defense and the Israeli Security Agency, chose to migrate to the cloud.
facts.quote: not permitted to restrict the types of services and information that the Government (including the Ministry of Defense and Israeli Security Agency) chooses to migrate

sources.title: Documents Contradict Google's Claims About Its Project Nimbus Contract With Israel
Google Worried It Couldn't Control How Israel Uses Project Nimbus, Files Reveal

facts.claim: On April 16, 2024 employees organized by the No Tech for Apartheid campaign held sit-ins at Google's New York office and Google Cloud offices in Sunnyvale, California, protesting Project Nimbus; nine were arrested. Google then fired 28 employees, saying in an internal memo that investigations had resulted in the terminations and that protesters had taken over office spaces, defaced property and impeded other employees' work. The campaign called the firings retaliation and said some of those fired had not participated.
facts.quote: individual investigations that resulted in the termination of employment for 28 employees, and will continue to investigate and take action as needed.

facts.claim: In January 2024 Palantir held its first board meeting of the year in Tel Aviv and announced a strategic partnership with the Israeli Ministry of Defense to supply technology to assist in the war; Palantir's 2024 quarterly report to the SEC describes the agreement in the same terms.
facts.quote: agreed to a strategic partnership with the Israeli Defense Ministry to supply technology to Israel to assist in the ongoing war

facts.claim: Palantir CEO Alex Karp told CNBC in March 2024 that within weeks of October 7, 2023 the company was on the ground in Israel and involved in operationally crucial operations, and that his outspoken pro-Israel views had led some employees to leave the company.
facts.quote: within weeks, we are on the ground and we are involved in operationally crucial operations in Israel

sources.title: Palantir CEO says his outspoken pro-Israel views have caused employees to leave company

facts.claim: On September 25, 2025 Microsoft vice chair Brad Smith said the company had ceased and disabled a set of services, including cloud storage and AI services, to a unit within the Israel Ministry of Defense, after an external review led by Covington & Burling found evidence supporting elements of an August 2025 Guardian report that Unit 8200 had used Azure to store and analyze civilian phone calls from the West Bank and Gaza. Microsoft said its cybersecurity work for Israel was not affected.
facts.quote: ceased and disabled a set of services to a unit within the Israel ministry of defense

facts.claim: A Calcalist-reported study of nearly 200 Israeli cybersecurity companies acquired over 15 years found that nearly half of the founders whose companies were acquired for more than $100 million in the past decade had served in the army's signals-intelligence Unit 8200.
facts.quote: nearly 50% of founders whose companies were acquired for over $100 million in the last decade served in the unit
